tEn: Sam Altman on Elon Musk, 'Artificial,' and the Future of Humanity (Part One)
tZh: 山姆·奥特曼谈埃隆·马斯克、《人造》与人类未来（上）
sEn: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman discusses AI's watershed moment, his public image, and the future of humanity in a candid Vanity Fair interview.
sZh: OpenAI 首席执行官山姆·奥特曼在《名利场》坦诚访谈中，探讨 AI 的转折点、他的公众形象与人类未来。

consensus.en: AGI is coming and most people now believe it, unlike a decade ago.
consensus.zh: AGI（通用人工智能）即将到来，与十年前不同，现在大多数人都相信这一点。

consensus.en: We must balance AI's risks and benefits, not stop technological progress.
consensus.zh: 我们必须平衡AI的风险与收益，而不是停止技术进步。

consensus.en: Companies and governments must cooperate on shared AI safety standards.
consensus.zh: 公司和政府必须合作制定共享的AI安全标准。

consensus.en: OpenAI will prioritize its mission over shareholder profits even after IPO.
consensus.zh: 即使上市后，OpenAI也会将使命置于股东利润之上。

consensus.en: AI can cure diseases like Alzheimer's and greatly improve human health.
consensus.zh: AI可以治愈阿尔茨海默病等疾病，并极大改善人类健康。

consensus.en: We need to slow down AI capabilities until alignment and safety catch up.
consensus.zh: 我们需要放慢AI能力的发展，直到对齐和安全措施跟上。

contrarian.en: Having kids didn't change my risk calculus; I was already cautious.
contrarian.zh: 生孩子并没有改变我的风险考量；我本来就很谨慎。

contrarian.en: Pronatalism as a trend to fight population decline is hard to understand.
contrarian.zh: 将鼓励生育作为对抗人口下降的趋势令人难以理解。

contrarian.en: I have no equity in OpenAI and think that was a mistake.
contrarian.zh: 我在OpenAI没有股权，并认为这是一个错误。

contrarian.en: AI is not related to my understanding of God; it's purely scientific.
contrarian.zh: AI与我对上帝的理解无关；它纯粹是科学。

contrarian.en: I'm incredibly optimistic about the future of AI, despite the risks.
contrarian.zh: 尽管存在风险，我对AI的未来极其乐观。

contrarian.en: Elon Musk is a bully, and sometimes you have to punch back.
contrarian.zh: 埃隆·马斯克是个恶霸，有时你必须回击。

turns.en: From Vanity Fair. This is Fair Game. I'm Mark Aduchi. Every day, a new scientific breakthrough or existential threat seems to make the world more aware, more anxious, and more distrusting of an AI future that we're told is rapidly approaching. And nobody is more recognized as the face of artificial intelligence, as a technology, an industry, and as a civilizational shift than OpenAI co-founder and CEO Sam Altman. For that reason, Sam Altman is on Vanity Fair's cover this month and sits at number one on our new establishment list. I sat down with Altman for two interviews in San Francisco. The first on September 11th and then again today, October 2nd. In those weeks, the story about AI seemed to turn upside down about half a dozen times. And over the course of our conversations, we discussed everything from Sam Altman's life, his children, his rivalries, pronatalism, prepping for the apocalypse, Luca Guadagnino's Artificial, and whether he thinks he's been mischaracterized as a villain in society. We talked about his company, his new products, the delayed IPO, his compensation, the recent exodus of OpenAI executives, and we talked about the technology itself, slowing down, government regulation, industry self-policing, President Xi Jinping's state visit and protecting human life, including in the case of suicide. I should note before we begin that Condé Nast, Vanity Fair's parent company, has a content licensing agreement with OpenAI. Both interviews with Altman are live now. This is part one.
turns.zh: 来自《名利场》。这里是 Fair Game。我是 Mark Aduchi。每天，似乎都有新的科学突破或生存威胁，让世界对那个据说正迅速逼近的 AI 未来更加警觉、更加焦虑、也更加不信任。而作为人工智能——无论是作为技术、产业还是文明转型——的代言人，没有人比 OpenAI 联合创始人兼 CEO Sam Altman 更受瞩目。正因如此，Sam Altman 登上了本月《名利场》的封面，并在我们的新权势榜上位列第一。我在旧金山与 Altman 进行了两次访谈。第一次在 9 月 11 日，然后就是今天，10 月 2 日。在这几周里，关于 AI 的叙事似乎翻来覆去变了五六次。在我们的对话中，我们聊了从 Sam Altman 的生活、他的孩子、他的竞争关系、鼓励生育、为末日做准备、Luca Guadagnino 的《Artificial》，到他是否觉得自己被社会错误地塑造成了反派。我们谈了他的公司、他的新产品、推迟的 IPO、他的薪酬、OpenAI 高管近期的离职潮，也谈了技术本身、放缓发展、政府监管、行业自律、习近平主席的国事访问，以及保护人命，包括自杀案例。开始前我要说明，《名利场》的母公司康泰纳仕与 OpenAI 有内容授权协议。两次 Altman 访谈现在都已上线。这是第一部分。

turns.en: Sam, it's good to see you.
turns.zh: Sam，很高兴见到你。

turns.en: You too.
turns.zh: 我也是。

turns.en: We are speaking at an extraordinary time, I think, for AI in terms of the capabilities and the risks and the public awareness of both. This feels like a watershed moment. And I just want to know, Sam, what has the past month been like for you? Have you slept? Is your phone ringing off the hook? Are world leaders calling you asking for answers? Does this feel like the 2022 moment when you launched ChatGPT where something has changed or is this just an average week in the life?
turns.zh: 我们正处在一个非凡的时刻，我认为，对 AI 而言，无论是能力、风险还是公众对两者的认知。这感觉像是一个分水岭。我只想知道，Sam，过去这一个月对你来说是什么样的？你睡过觉吗？电话是不是响个不停？各国领导人是不是都在打电话找你寻求答案？这感觉像 2022 年你推出 ChatGPT 的那个时刻，有些东西已经改变，还是只是你生活中普通的一周？

turns.en: A little bit of both, to be honest. I think the internal experience of this is we have been talking about this and preparing for this for the last decade in some sense. And we have been seeing this exponential progress and we have been confused about why more of the world has not seen progress the way that we've seen it because to us the fact that this moment would come has been very predictable.
turns.zh: 说实话，两者都有一点。我想，从内部体验来说，某种意义上，过去十年我们一直在谈论这件事、为此做准备。我们一直看到这种指数级的进步，也一直困惑为什么世界上更多人没有像我们这样看到进步，因为对我们来说，这一刻会到来是非常可预测的。

turns.en: Do you feel like you understand how frightened people are out there right now and do you feel a need to reassure people or help them understand it?
turns.zh: 你觉得你理解现在外面的人有多害怕吗？你觉得有必要安抚人们，或者帮助他们理解这件事吗？

turns.en: Of course. Yes to both.
turns.zh: 当然。两个都是肯定的。

turns.en: Yes to both.
turns.zh: 两个都是肯定的。

turns.en: If you go back 10 years and read what we talked about when we started the company it matches this moment very well. Now the difference is 10 years ago very few people believed us now most people believe us.
turns.zh: 如果你回到 10 年前，读读我们创办公司时谈的内容，和此刻非常吻合。区别在于，10 年前很少有人相信我们，现在大多数人都相信我们了。

turns.en: Both that AGI is coming and
turns.zh: 既相信 AGI 会到来，也

turns.en: Is it here?
turns.zh: 它已经来了吗？

turns.en: It's subjective, right?
turns.zh: 这是主观的，对吧？

turns.en: It's subjective, yeah, it's close. I think you could say we've been very successful at kind of what we set out to do and now we're going through a recalibration and a kind of like a period where society is like okay this is coming now society is still continuing much the same we have this incredible new thing and I think it's very fair to say the world hasn't changed that much and you know I think a criticism that we got we still get but less recently is you said that you said you were going to do these amazing things and like where's the impact on the world. You know, where's the economic growth? Where's the cure for cancer? Where's the this?
turns.zh: 是主观的，对，很接近了。我想可以说，我们在最初设定的目标上非常成功，现在我们正经历一次重新校准，一个社会说“好，这要来了”的阶段，而社会大体上仍在照常运转，我们有了这个不可思议的新东西，而且我认为很公平地说，世界并没有改变那么多。你知道，我们曾受到、现在仍受到但最近少一些的一个批评是：你说过你要做这些了不起的事，那对世界的影响在哪？经济增长在哪？癌症的解药在哪？这个那个在哪？

turns.en: And yet it does feel like something important is changing.
turns.zh: 然而确实感觉有些重要的东西正在改变。

turns.en: We are one player of many, but we want to, you know, work with all of the other stakeholders in society.
turns.zh: 我们是众多参与者之一，但我们想，你知道，与社会中所有其他利益相关方合作。

turns.en: You are one player of many, but you specifically, Sam, are in many ways the human face of artificial intelligence. You got there first and you became the brand as a person and as a company. And I think it's fair to say if it's the Manhattan Project, you're the Oppenheimer.
turns.zh: 你是众多参与者之一，但特别是你，Sam，在很多方面是人工智能的人类面孔。你先到了那里，你作为个人和公司成了品牌。我认为很公平地说，如果这是曼哈顿计划，你就是奥本海默。

turns.en: I wouldn't be the first person to say that. And I'm curious just what does that feel like?
turns.zh: 我不是第一个这么说的人。我很好奇那是什么感觉？

turns.en: I will answer that. This is not me trying to brush it aside or like false modesty or anything, but the degree to which this is a collective effort, but mostly that this is about a story of, you know, a relatively small number of brilliant scientists and engineers that did something amazing. And much less a story about me I think is not well understood. I think there are many people that could have done the part of this that I did and the kind of key researchers and engineers and I think they are recognized at this point but it is like it is one of the most important and impressive and impactful things that we've seen in a very long time in any in any scientific or engineering discipline. Kevin Roo's book does a good the new book does a good job of bringing out some of the supporting parts.
turns.zh: 我会回答。这不是我想搪塞过去，也不是假谦虚之类的，而是这在多大程度上是集体努力，但主要是，这是一个关于相对少数杰出科学家和工程师做了了不起事情的故事。而远不是我个人的故事，我认为这一点没有被很好地理解。我认为有很多人可以完成我做的这部分，那些关键的研究人员和工程师，我认为他们现在得到了认可，但这是我们在任何科学或工程学科中很长时间以来见过的最重要、最令人印象深刻、最具影响力的事情之一。Kevin Roo 的新书很好地呈现了一些配角部分。

turns.en: It is true that I got, you know, as much as anybody or more than anybody else like the face of this whole thing. And the sink for all the a lot of the anxiety and fear and everything else. But it is it is a strange experience to say the least.
turns.zh: 确实，你知道，我像任何人一样、甚至比任何人更多地成了这整件事的面孔。也成了很多焦虑、恐惧和其他一切的宣泄口。但至少可以说，这是一种奇怪的体验。

turns.en: I think you could you're saying this, I will go further. I think a lot of people at this moment see AI as an evil force and because of your association with it from the jump, you're seen as a villain, do you feel you've been mischaracterized? Is that frustrating to you?
turns.zh: 我想你可以——你这么说，我要更进一步。我认为此刻很多人把 AI 视为一种邪恶力量，而因为你从一开始就与之关联，你被视为反派。你觉得你被错误地刻画了吗？这让你沮丧吗？

turns.en: I do feel I've been mischaracterized. It's only somewhat frustrating.
turns.zh: 我确实觉得我被错误地刻画了。只是有点沮丧。

turns.en: Okay.
turns.zh: 好。

turns.en: I think if there were somebody else doing my job, people would have the same feelings and say the same things that probably wouldn't resonate with that person. I think it's not really about the specific person. It is that people need a sink for the anxiety, a scapegoat, a just like, man, this change is happening to the world.
turns.zh: 我认为如果是别人做我的工作，人们也会有同样的感受、说同样的话，只是可能不会和那个人产生共鸣。我认为这其实不是关于具体某个人。而是人们需要一个焦虑的宣泄口、一个替罪羊，就像，天哪，这种变化正在降临世界。

turns.en: So you can divorce a person.
turns.zh: 所以你可以把人和事分开。

turns.en: You can divorce it from how you feel about yourself.
turns.zh: 你可以把它和你对自己的感受分开。

turns.en: I take it somewhat personally, but not that personally. Like I I understand the human instinct here. I have felt this way towards other people in previous eras of technology.
turns.zh: 我有点往心里去，但没那么往心里去。我理解这里的人类本能。在以前的技术时代，我也曾对别人有过这种感觉。

turns.en: I feel bad about it now. But I think I get the human instinct. Who was that?
turns.zh: 我现在为此感到抱歉。但我想我理解这种人类本能。那是谁？

turns.en: Well, one example of someone that I know personally that I'll talk about is like Mark Zuckerberg. I had like a very evil caricature of him in my head in the early days of Meta. I didn't know him at the time. I know him not super well, but I know him now. I think I was like projecting whatever people project onto someone with what they perceive is too much power and influence over the world.
turns.zh: 嗯，我亲自认识、愿意谈的一个例子是 Mark Zuckerberg。在 Meta 早期，我脑子里对他有一个非常邪恶的漫画式形象。当时我不认识他。我和他不是很熟，但我现在认识他。我想我当时是在投射人们投射到某个他们认为对世界拥有过多权力和影响力的人身上的东西。

turns.en: Sam, you are a parent of two. I don't have kids, but all of my friends who do talk about how having kids dramatically changes how they think about the future.
turns.zh: Sam，你是两个孩子的家长。我没有孩子，但我所有有孩子的朋友都说，有孩子会极大地改变他们对未来的思考方式。

turns.en: I can only imagine that's truer for you as someone who probably understands our future a lot better than most, and has a unique role in shaping it. Has having kids changed how you do your job?
turns.zh: 我只能想象，对你这样可能比大多数人更了解我们的未来、又在塑造未来上有独特角色的人来说，这一点更是如此。有了孩子之后，你做工作的方式变了吗？

turns.en: Yes, but probably not in the way that you would expect, or maybe you might expect. Having kids is by far the best thing I've ever done. I feel very blessed to have had many wonderful things happen to me in my life, but having kids is the number one by a huge margin. Everything people told me, including that you can't really understand how good it is, has all been true. It is the most amazing, greatest blessing, most fun thing ever. I was very intent on not destroying the world before having kids. I didn't need kids to be like, okay, I really shouldn't gamble with the future of civilization. And I am somewhat surprised about the number of people who have said, oh, I'm really happy you have kids because now you won't take crazy catastrophic risk for all of us. Like, I wasn't going to do that anyway. But in terms of the premium I put on being away from my kids to do anything else, it's been wonderfully focusing from the perspective of what I actually care about and want to prioritize. And then watching the way kids experience the world and thinking about, obviously we don't want to destroy the world, but what do we want to preserve and what kind of world do we want to build, and what are these magical human experiences, and how do we want kids to use this technology and be able to have agency and develop their creativity and everything else.
turns.zh: 变了，但可能不是你会预期的那种方式，或者也许你也能猜到。有孩子是我这辈子做过的最好的事，远远超过其他一切。我觉得自己非常幸运，人生中发生过很多美好的事，但有孩子是第一名，而且遥遥领先。人们告诉我的所有话，包括“你没法真正理解这有多好”，全都是真的。这是最奇妙、最大的福气、最有趣的事。在有孩子之前，我就非常坚定地不想毁掉世界。我不需要有孩子才会觉得，好吧，我真的不该拿文明的未来去赌。我有点惊讶，居然有那么多人说，哦，我很高兴你有孩子了，因为这样你就不会为我们所有人去冒那种疯狂的灾难性风险了。可我本来也不会那么做。但说到我为了做别的事而离开孩子所付出的代价，从“我真正在乎什么、想优先什么”的角度看，这反而让我非常专注。然后看着孩子体验世界的方式，去想：我们显然不想毁掉世界，但我们想保留什么、想建设什么样的世界、这些神奇的人类体验是什么，以及我们希望孩子如何使用这项技术，能够拥有能动性、发展创造力等等。

turns.en: So when do you think you'll start to introduce them to AI? It brings up questions that one would ask for themselves, but takes on different resonance when it's for your children.
turns.zh: 那你觉得你什么时候会开始让他们接触 AI？这些问题人们也会问自己，但放到自己孩子身上，共鸣就不一样了。

turns.en: I mean, everyone's going to make their own decisions about their own kids, but I'm a big fan of limiting technology across the board for kids. I think it's good for kids to be running around outside and playing in nature and doing whatever kids have done for a long time. I don't think we understand all of the impacts of technology on small children, for good or for bad. But as a parent making decisions for my own kids, I will certainly say when I watch kids that are glued to a touchscreen of some sort, scrolling through brain rot short form video, I have a strong instinct that that's a bad thing.
turns.zh: 每个人都会为自己的孩子做自己的决定，但我非常赞成对孩子全面限制技术。我觉得孩子就该在外面跑来跑去、在大自然里玩，做孩子们长期以来一直在做的事。我不认为我们完全理解技术对幼儿的影响，无论是好是坏。但作为一个为自己孩子做决定的家长，我肯定会说，当我看到孩子们黏在某种触摸屏上、刷着那种“脑腐”短视频时，我强烈地觉得那是件坏事。

turns.en: Mhm.
turns.zh: 嗯。

turns.en: And I mean, it may be a bad thing for adults too.
turns.zh: 而且我的意思是，对成年人来说可能也是坏事。

turns.en: I was going to say, adults do that too.
turns.zh: 我正想说，成年人也这样。

turns.en: But something about a developing brain seems especially important to protect from new technology we don't fully understand. And I feel the same way about AI. Clearly kids born today are going to grow up in a world with AI and need to be able to use it. I doubt early childhood is the right point for that. I don't have an age in mind where I would let my kids talk to ChatGPT yet, but it is certainly not now.
turns.zh: 但发育中的大脑，似乎尤其需要保护，免受我们尚未完全理解的新技术影响。我对 AI 也是同样的感觉。显然，今天出生的孩子会在一个有 AI 的世界里长大，也需要会用它。我怀疑幼儿期是不是合适的起点。我还没有想好一个年龄，说到了那时我会让孩子跟 ChatGPT 对话，但肯定不是现在。

turns.en: You said that you like having kids. I wonder, do you plan to have more?
turns.zh: 你说你喜欢有孩子。我想知道，你打算再要更多吗？

turns.en: Yes. Yes. Yeah.
turns.zh: 是的。是的。对。

turns.en: How many, do you know?
turns.zh: 多少个，你知道吗？

turns.en: Even going to two kids, I remember Ollie and I were talking about this. It's so hard to split time, because you want to be there for everything. You want to spend so much time with them. So with unlimited time, I would want to have so many kids, but I want to be so present for each one of them. And I know Ali feels the same, that that will be the limit. But given unlimited time, I would want to have a lot of kids, and given limited time, it will not be an army of kids.
turns.zh: 就算只是要两个孩子，我记得我和 Ollie 聊过这个。时间真的很难分配，因为你想参与每一件事，想花很多时间陪他们。所以如果有无限的时间，我会想生很多孩子，但我也想对每一个孩子都非常投入。我知道 Ali 也是这么想的，那就会是限制所在。但如果有无限时间，我会想要很多孩子；而时间有限的话，就不会是一支孩子大军。

turns.en: There's a trend out here in Silicon Valley about pronatalism and about having more kids to combat population decline. Is that...
turns.zh: 硅谷这边有一种“鼓励生育”的趋势，说要多生孩子来对抗人口下降。那是……

turns.en: I just find that tough to understand as a trend. I love our kids so much and I know I'll have more kids, but there's no part of it which is like, we gotta fight against population decline. I just love a big family. It's really great.
turns.zh: 我只是觉得，作为一种趋势，这很难理解。我非常爱我们的孩子，我也知道我会再要孩子，但其中没有任何一部分是“我们得对抗人口下降”。我就是喜欢大家庭。真的很棒。

turns.en: So Sam, you're about to get the biopic treatment in Luca Guadagnino's Artificial.
turns.zh: 那么 Sam，你即将在 Luca Guadagnino 的《Artificial》里被拍成传记片。

turns.en: Oh yeah.
turns.zh: 哦，对。

turns.en: Oh yeah. Have you seen the trailer?
turns.zh: 哦，对。你看过预告片吗？

turns.en: I did see the trailer.
turns.zh: 我看过预告片。

turns.en: Okay. What'd you think?
turns.zh: 好。你觉得怎么样？

turns.en: He did walk like me. Actually, I'll tell you something. They filmed outside of our house. There were these notices on our street that there was going to be some filming or whatever. I didn't realize what was going on. I paid no attention. And then one morning I was walking down the street to get coffee and there were all these cameras and there was a guy dressed exactly like me with my same backpack, walking like me so much that I felt I was in some weird glitch of the simulation or something. It was very strange. And then I immediately figured out what was happening. We waved and went on. But it was really weird, and it's a strange thing to see someone that has nailed your quirky mannerisms or whatever. Surreal. But you haven't spoken to Andrew Garfield or anything.
turns.zh: 他走路确实像我。其实我跟你说件事。他们在我家外面拍摄。我们那条街上贴了通知，说会有拍摄之类的。我当时没意识到是怎么回事，完全没在意。然后有一天早上，我沿街走去买咖啡，那里全是摄像机，还有一个人穿得跟我一模一样，背着和我一样的背包，走路也特别像我，以至于我觉得自己像是掉进了模拟世界里的某种诡异故障。非常奇怪。然后我立刻明白了发生了什么。我们挥了挥手就走了。但那真的很怪，看到有人把你那些古怪的小动作都抓得那么准，是种很奇怪的感觉。超现实。不过你还没跟 Andrew Garfield 说过话之类的吧。

turns.en: I waved at him that one time.
turns.zh: 我那次朝他挥了挥手。

turns.en: He waved at him that one time.
turns.zh: 他那次朝他挥了挥手。

turns.en: Amazon produced that movie, but back in June they announced that they wouldn't distribute it. And so it was sold to Neon and they're going to put it out on Christmas Day. Earlier this year, Amazon invested $50 billion into OpenAI. You can see how that could look. Sam, did you or anyone on your behalf speak to anyone at Amazon about it?
turns.zh: 那部电影是 Amazon 制作的，但他们在六月宣布不会发行它。所以它被卖给了 Neon，他们将在圣诞节上映。今年早些时候，Amazon 向 OpenAI 投资了 500 亿美元。你能看出这看起来会是什么样。Sam，你或你这边有没有任何人跟 Amazon 的人谈过这件事？

turns.en: I did not, and I don't know of anyone else who did.
turns.zh: 我没有，我也不知道还有谁谈过。

turns.en: Okay. You never spoke to Jeff Bezos about it?
turns.zh: 好。你从没跟 Jeff Bezos 谈过这件事？

turns.en: All right. I haven't seen the film, but I'm told it's a dark portrait. That doesn't bother you, to be portrayed that way. It doesn't feel like you want to correct the record on something. I will say, from having watched the trailer, I don't think they're going for accuracy.
turns.zh: 好吧。我还没看过这部电影，但有人告诉我它是一幅阴暗的画像。被那样描绘，你不在意吗？感觉你并不想去纠正什么记录。我要说的是，从看过预告片来看，我不觉得他们在追求准确性。

turns.en: Okay.
turns.zh: 好。

turns.en: So in that sense, no, it doesn't bother me. I mean, they're trying to make a good movie, and maybe it will be good. I don't know.
turns.zh: 所以从这个意义上说，不，我不介意。我的意思是，他们是在努力拍一部好电影，也许它会不错。我不知道。

turns.en: Okay. Good as a movie.
turns.zh: 好。作为电影来说不错。

turns.en: It will not be good as an accurate depiction.
turns.zh: 作为准确的描绘，它不会好。

turns.en: Okay. Except for the walk.
turns.zh: 好。除了走路。

turns.en: Except that seemed good. I'm sure they'll get some other parts right, at least accidentally.
turns.zh: 除了那个看起来不错。我相信他们也会把其他一些部分弄对，至少是碰巧弄对。

turns.en: So there's a moment in the trailer where the character of Sam Altman walks into kind of a James Bond sort of bunker and there's firearms on the wall.
turns.zh: 预告片里有一个时刻，Sam Altman 的角色走进一个类似詹姆斯·邦德式的掩体，墙上挂着枪械。

turns.en: That's an example of an inaccuracy, but I did look kind of cool. I mean, so that's inaccurate.
turns.zh: 那就是一个不准确的例子，但看起来确实挺酷的。我的意思是，那是不准确的。

turns.en: There's no bunker with firearms on the wall.
turns.zh: 并没有那种墙上挂着枪械的地堡。

turns.en: I was going to ask, are you a prepper? That's another trend out here that back in New York we find curious.
turns.zh: 我正想问，你是末日准备者吗？这是这里的另一个潮流，在纽约我们觉得挺好奇的。

turns.en: I have a survivalist mindset, I would say.
turns.zh: 我会说，我有一种生存主义的心态。

turns.en: Okay.
turns.zh: 好。

turns.en: And I am intellectually interested in that stuff, but I don't have a setup like is depicted in that trailer.
turns.zh: 我在智识上对这类东西感兴趣，但我并没有那个预告片里描绘的那种配置。

turns.en: Do you have a bugout plan?
turns.zh: 你有撤离计划吗？

turns.en: I mean, like at our ranch, we can survive off-grid, which I guess to many people would be considered a bugout plan.
turns.zh: 我是说，比如在我们的牧场，我们可以离网生存，我猜对很多人来说这就算撤离计划了。

turns.en: Okay. But it's not like
turns.zh: 好。但并不是说

turns.en: we don't have like a submarine
turns.zh: 我们没有潜艇

turns.en: a go bag with like a plan for a helicopter and
turns.zh: 一个应急包，里面有直升机计划之类的

turns.en: no helicopter, no submarine
turns.zh: 没有直升机，没有潜艇

turns.en: because this idea of prepping I think feels terrifying to normal Americans where they're not only is that not an option for most people but it feels like a mindset that they didn't know they were supposed to have.
turns.zh: 因为这种准备的想法，我觉得对普通美国人来说很可怕，不仅对大多数人来说这不是一个选项，而且这感觉像是一种他们不知道自己本该有的心态。

turns.en: When COVID came, I had like a big stack of masks ready to go and I had like enough canned food in the house that if like the world had shut down, we could have like had enough food for a while and we had like water purification tablets and I remember a friend of mine said like, I used to make fun of you for that stuff. That was like probably something that was like very reasonable to do.
turns.zh: 新冠来的时候，我有一大堆口罩准备好了，家里有足够的罐头食品，如果世界停摆，我们也能撑一阵子，我们还有净水片，我记得一个朋友说，我以前还拿这些事取笑你。那大概是很合理的做法。

turns.en: AI aside, like we have I do think we underprepare for these sort of like unusual events like COVID and after COVID I would have expected more people to say like okay
turns.zh: 撇开 AI 不谈，我确实认为我们对这类不寻常事件准备不足，比如新冠，新冠之后我本以为会有更多人说，好吧

turns.en: maybe it is worth like 0.1% more effort of my like effort in my life to like be ready for the next pandemic or whatever. And I don't think most people updated on that and it's like slightly strange to me. I don't have masks in my apartment anymore.
turns.zh: 也许值得在我生活中多花 0.1% 的精力，为下一次大流行之类的做好准备。我不认为大多数人更新了这一点，这对我来说有点奇怪。我公寓里现在没有口罩了。

turns.en: And maybe you should.
turns.zh: 也许你应该有。

turns.en: Sure. And maybe I should.
turns.zh: 当然。也许我应该有。

turns.en: So Sam, you and your peers in AI, I think, are assuming roles that go beyond business leaders. I know that at one point you were contemplating the idea of running for governor of California. That
turns.zh: 那么 Sam，你和你在 AI 领域的同行们，我认为正在承担超越商业领袖的角色。我知道你曾一度考虑竞选加州州长。那

turns.en: a little bit. I guess it's like overstated, but yes, a little bit is true.
turns.zh: 有一点。我猜这被夸大了，但没错，有一点是真的。

turns.en: And then in Keach's biography, she says that you contemplated the idea of the presidency. And I just want to ask for the record, do you have any current plans to run for office?
turns.zh: 然后在基奇的传记里，她说你考虑过竞选总统。我只想正式问一下，你目前有任何竞选公职的计划吗？

turns.en: No.
turns.zh: 没有。

turns.en: Is the presidency still something you would ever consider?
turns.zh: 总统职位仍然是你可能会考虑的事情吗？

turns.en: No. And I don't think that I dispute the accuracy of that one. The governor thing is true.
turns.zh: 不。我不认为我质疑那件事的准确性。州长那件事是真的。

turns.en: Okay.
turns.zh: 好。

turns.en: I do not ever plan to run for office. I think I have gotten enough of a taste of what that would be like in my current role to know that it's not something I would want.
turns.zh: 我从不打算竞选公职。我想我在目前的角色中已经足够尝到了那会是什么样子，知道那不是我想要的。

turns.en: What do you think about the governorship that attracted you in the first place?
turns.zh: 最初吸引你的是州长职位的哪一点？

turns.en: Well, I love California and I think that it is like a very badly managed state on the whole and I think that there's maybe a limited amount any governor could do about that.
turns.zh: 嗯，我爱加州，我认为总体而言它是一个管理得很糟糕的州，我认为任何州长能做的可能都有限。

turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 是的。

turns.en: But I thought it would be fun to at least try. I think AI is way more important.
turns.zh: 但我觉得至少试一试会很有趣。我认为 AI 重要得多。

turns.en: You've talked about being a spiritual person before. I'm wondering how does AGI relate to your understanding of God?
turns.zh: 你之前谈过自己是一个有灵性的人。我想知道 AGI 与你对上帝的理解有何关系？

turns.en: Not at all.
turns.zh: 完全没关系。

turns.en: Not at all.
turns.zh: 完全没关系。

turns.en: No.
turns.zh: 没有。

turns.en: Elaborate.
turns.zh: 详细说说。

turns.en: I think AI is something inside the realm of science and well understood or becoming more well understood and it is a it is like a
turns.zh: 我认为 AI 是科学领域内的东西，已经被很好地理解，或者正在被更好地理解，它是一个，它就像一个

turns.en: actually I'll leave it there.
turns.zh: 其实我就说到这里吧。

turns.en: Do you think that this is your fate or your destiny?
turns.zh: 你认为这是你的命运或天命吗？

turns.en: No, I think I could have done many things and I kind of been pretty happy with any of them.
turns.zh: 不，我认为我本可以做很多事情，而且我对其中任何一件都会挺满意的。

turns.en: Okay.
turns.zh: 好。

turns.en: But I'm very I feel very grateful and lucky to get to work on this. It's like a It's like a great privilege.
turns.zh: 但我非常，我感到非常感激和幸运能从事这项工作。这就像一个，这是一种巨大的荣幸。

turns.en: But it's is it almost an inevitability that AI was going to happen and you get to be the person that leads it?
turns.zh: 但 AI 的发生几乎是不可避免的，而你恰好成为引领它的人？

turns.en: I think it's an inevitability that it was going to happen. I mean it's just like human effort and human society collectively builds towards technological progress. But it is like kind of chancy and lucky that I got to be one of the people involved.
turns.zh: 我认为它的发生是不可避免的。我的意思是，这就像人类的努力和人类社会集体朝着技术进步前进。但我能成为参与其中的人之一，多少有点偶然和幸运。

turns.en: Yeah. In that Kevin Roose book I mentioned before, he talks about how Oppenheimer in the 50s in hearings, he talked about how even when he saw what nuclear science could do that they saw it also as technically sweet and it was like something that he felt compelled to there was something human about when you can see it's possible, it's like putting the last puzzle piece into the puzzle no matter what the picture is.
turns.zh: 是的。在我之前提到的凯文·鲁斯那本书里，他谈到奥本海默在 50 年代的听证会上，他说即使当他看到核科学能做什么时，他们也觉得它在技术上很美妙，那是一种他觉得不得不做的事，当你看到它可能实现时，有一种人性的东西，就像把最后一块拼图放进拼图里，不管那幅画是什么。

turns.en: I did feel that. I remember feeling something very similar to that which is that like early in AI it was like the number of incredible difficult like hardfought pieces of science and engineering that had to come together to let all of us be able to do this this next thing in this moment.
turns.zh: 我确实有那种感觉。我记得有过非常相似的感受，就是在 AI 早期，有那么多极其困难、来之不易的科学和工程片段必须汇聚在一起，才能让我们所有人能够在此刻做这下一件事。

turns.en: Mhm.
turns.zh: 嗯。

turns.en: And that really struck me, but I don't think of it as like a final puzzle piece because there's going to be many things that come next and people will be like, "Oh, that was one of the ingredients I needed to do this much more amazing thing."
turns.zh: 那真的打动了我，但我不认为它是最后一块拼图，因为接下来还会有很多事情，人们会说，“哦，那是我做这件更了不起的事情所需的原料之一。”

turns.en: Now, I want to talk about your company. So, OpenAI was famously founded as a nonprofit and then converted to a for-profit structure so as to raise capital for the huge amounts of compute and expensive talent that it was required to stay competitive. Now you're preparing an IPO. When you go public, your company's incentive structure will, like any public company, be tied to profit maximization and shareholder value. Are you nervous about what going public will do to the soul of the company?
turns.zh: 现在，我想谈谈你的公司。OpenAI 众所周知最初是一个非营利组织，后来转为营利结构，以便筹集资金来获得保持竞争力所需的大量算力和昂贵人才。现在你们正在准备 IPO。当你们上市时，公司的激励结构会像任何上市公司一样，与利润最大化和股东价值挂钩。你是否担心上市会对公司的灵魂造成什么影响？

turns.en: First of all, we will not be like any other company. Even when we go public, which we are not in a rush to do, we will still have a nonprofit that governs us. We will remind investors and anyone that thinks about buying our shares that we are going to put the mission first. We believe that that will be compatible with our shareholders doing super well. I genuinely do think that. But if they are ever in tension, the mission is going to come first and if we have to do something that is in the interest of the world but not our particular shareholders, it's going to be very easy about what we're going to decide to do there. And that makes us I think different than most companies and people will decide if they're willing to sign up for that.
turns.zh: 首先，我们不会像任何其他公司一样。即使我们上市——我们并不急于上市——我们仍会有一个非营利组织来管理我们。我们会提醒投资者以及任何考虑购买我们股票的人，我们会把使命放在第一位。我们相信这与我们的股东表现极好是兼容的。我真的这么认为。但如果它们发生冲突，使命将优先，如果我们必须做符合世界利益但不符合我们特定股东利益的事情，我们会很容易决定怎么做。我认为这让我们与大多数公司不同，人们会决定他们是否愿意接受这一点。

turns.en: So, you're not worried that market demands will impact product safety?
turns.zh: 所以，你不担心市场需求会影响产品安全吗？

turns.en: I'm not. I don't. Well, that's not fair. I always worry about this kind of stuff, but I am confident we will make the right decision because we worry about it.
turns.zh: 我不担心。我不。嗯，这么说不太公平。我总是担心这类事情，但我有信心我们会做出正确的决定，因为我们担心它。

turns.en: Where tech companies that came before you failed.
turns.zh: 在你之前的科技公司在哪里失败了。

turns.en: They got some things right and a lot of things wrong. And we'll try to learn, but I'm sure we'll get our own things wrong, too. But we'll at least try not to make the same mistakes.
turns.zh: 他们做对一些事情，也做错了很多事情。我们会尝试学习，但我确信我们也会犯自己的错误。但至少我们会努力不犯同样的错误。

turns.en: As you pointed out at the beginning of this conversation, the world recognizes the stakes and the magnitude of this time. And I'm confident that we will have the support of people including our shareholders, employees, investors, partners in making the decisions that we believe are best for humanity's shared interests. Even if it means we are going slower on revenue than we otherwise could. We've been making decisions like this. We've slowed down.
turns.zh: 正如你在这次对话开头指出的，世界已经认识到这件事的利害关系和这个时刻的分量。我相信我们会得到包括股东、员工、投资者、合作伙伴在内的支持，去做出我们认为最符合人类共同利益的决定。即使这意味着我们的营收增长会比原本可能的速度更慢。我们一直在做这样的决定。我们放慢了脚步。

turns.en: How does that work though if your stock price starts to fall because you're not hitting your profit benchmarks that you need to? What happens then?
turns.zh: 但如果因为达不到所需的利润基准，股价开始下跌，那又该怎么办？到时候会发生什么？

turns.en: Then it falls. Maybe it falls a lot. I don't know. And again, we will try to continue to communicate very clearly that if there is ever a question about our share price going up or doing the right thing for the future of humanity, we are not going to pay attention to the share price in that moment. If we have patient investors, I think they'll be very happy over time, but quarter to quarter probably going to be very volatile and we're going to have to make some hard decisions. That is part of the reason I think we'll be very successful over time. But if we are wrong about that, and for some reason AI progress is incompatible with making an incredibly valuable company—I really don't think it's the case. I really think these are compatible. We are clearly going to pick doing the right thing for humanity.
turns.zh: 那就跌吧。也许跌得很惨。我不知道。再说一次，我们会继续非常清楚地表明：如果有一天要在股价上涨和为人类未来做正确的事之间做选择，那一刻我们不会去关注股价。如果我们有耐心的投资者，我想长期来看他们会非常满意，但逐季来看可能会非常波动，我们将不得不做出一些艰难的决定。这也是我认为我们长期会非常成功的原因之一。但如果我们错了，如果出于某种原因，AI 的进步与打造一家极有价值的公司不相容——我真的不认为会这样。我真的认为这两者是相容的。我们显然会选择为人类做正确的事。

turns.en: Okay. And I think we've got a long track record if you look at the very first capital we raised of treating this with seriousness and we've paid all of these prices for having a crazy complex structure basically for this moment.
turns.zh: 好吧。如果你看看我们最早筹集的第一笔资金，我认为我们有着长期认真对待这件事的记录，我们为拥有一个极其复杂的结构付出了所有这些代价，基本上就是为了这一刻。

turns.en: Sam, is it right that you currently hold zero equity?
turns.zh: Sam，你现在持有零股权，对吗？

turns.en: Yeah, I have no direct equity. I have this tiny tiny sliver of exposure from an old YC investment.
turns.zh: 是的，我没有直接股权。我只有一笔来自旧 YC 投资的极小极小的一点敞口。

turns.en: So that doesn't make sense to most people who would think that if you're creating so much value in the world, you would deserve to participate in it. So how do you hope to be compensated?
turns.zh: 所以这对大多数人来说说不通，他们会认为如果你在世界上创造了这么多价值，你应该有权参与其中。那么你希望如何获得报酬？

turns.en: If I could go back and do things over again, I thought I was doing this thing that would—at the time, no one took AI that seriously, right? And so they looked at me then and said, 'What? This is crazy. You're going to work super hard and create all this value and not try to get richer. That's unimaginable.' Now I think all of a sudden more people sort of understand the rationale. And yet still people are like, you know, it just feels so out of—
turns.zh: 如果我能回到过去重新来过，我以为我在做的这件事——当时没有人那么认真地对待 AI，对吧？所以他们当时看着我说：‘什么？这太疯狂了。你要拼命工作，创造所有这些价值，却不试图变得更富有。这简直不可想象。’现在我觉得突然之间有更多人理解了其中的道理。但人们仍然觉得，你知道，这感觉太不——

turns.en: The rationale being that you've invested in other companies that will—
turns.zh: 道理是说你投资了其他公司，那些公司会——

turns.en: Oh no, the rationale being like, you know, we actually want you to just be making decisions on behalf of humanity and not financial interest.
turns.zh: 哦不，道理是说，你知道，我们其实希望你只代表人类做决定，而不是为了财务利益。

turns.en: Compensation.
turns.zh: 报酬。

turns.en: Yeah. I think it was a mistake and a lack of understanding of how most people think about the world. And weirdly, this big trust-destroying thing to not have equity.
turns.zh: 是的。我认为这是一个错误，也是缺乏对大多数人如何看待世界的理解。而且奇怪的是，没有股权反而成了一件严重破坏信任的事。

turns.en: How do you think about money? Some people think of it as a reward. Some people think about it as fuel to make something happen. Some people think of it as a safety net that they hoard.
turns.zh: 你怎么看待金钱？有些人把它看作奖励。有些人把它看作让事情发生的燃料。有些人把它看作他们囤积的安全网。

turns.en: I had a super successful career. I used to be extremely money motivated. So I'm not trying to say that I'm like, 'Oh, I just don't care. I'm like a monk.' I like nice stuff. I have expensive taste by any reasonable stance. But I had a super successful career and there's not more stuff that I want. Now I think it is fair that you can use money to do more projects and if I had had crazy amounts of money and hadn't had to raise money for OpenAI because I could have just self-funded it, I guess that would have been really nice. But I don't know. I think that this is why I wish I had just taken the stock. There's no way to say like 'I have so much money that there's not more stuff I want' that comes across as in any way relatable or not like you—so I wish I just had the equity. I don't know.

turns.en: Okay. So that brings us to the idea of slowing down. As I understand, you can't slow down because your competitors won't slow down and China won't slow down.
